fullName: 3D Micro & Nano Diffraction, depth-resolved polychromatic and monochromatic diffraction

status2026.detail: The APS commissioning chart dated 5 October 2026 places '34-ID-E: 3DMN XSD' at stage 5, 'Scientific Commissioning and Early Experiments'. General-user restart is stage 6. The proposal-types page updated 7 October nevertheless accepts General User and Rapid Access proposals for 34-ID-E. In January 2025, construction was scheduled after the other seven feature beamlines. The August update listed technical commissioning with early-2026 experiments expected. The 26 January 2026 chart still listed technical commissioning, stage 4. The upgrade project received final Department of Energy approval, CD-4, in January 2026. At the 12 to 14 August 2026 ModSim workshop at Brookhaven, the coded-aperture team reported early two-dimensional experiments around late July following a shutdown from mid-2023. Computing-intensive three-dimensional coded-aperture experiments were planned for winter. A new detector with about ten times faster collection was also planned.

tagline: Researchers map crystal orientation and strain within materials in three dimensions using a focused multi-energy X-ray beam.
summary: Metals, rocks and microchips contain crystals called grains. Grain orientation and strain affect properties such as fracture resistance and electrical performance. At 34-ID-E, researchers use 3D Micro & Nano Diffraction, 3DMN, to map these quantities in three dimensions. X-rays over roughly 5 to 30 keV are focused by mirrors into a design spot about 100 nm wide. The design spot at the second station is 40 nm. Each grain diffracts wavelengths determined by its atomic spacing and orientation. A detector about half a metre above the sample records the resulting Laue pattern. A platinum wire or patterned gold mask is scanned near the surface. From changes in the transmitted diffraction, researchers distinguish signals from different depths. As of October 2026, 3DMN is in scientific commissioning, with summer early experiments and general-user proposals accepted.

whatAPSUEnables.text: The focal spot includes a demagnified image of the X-ray source. In the design brightness mode, horizontal source width falls about nineteenfold, from 280 to 14.7 µm root-mean-square, and vertical width falls about threefold. The old mirrors required a 60 µm opening for a roughly 500 nm focus. More accurate new surfaces accept the full beam for design spots near 100 nm and 40 nm. These sizes are intended to resolve strain within dislocation walls in deformed metals. Increased coherence also permits three-dimensional imaging of individual grains. Design gains include a hundredfold brightness increase, ninefold mirror improvement, fivefold reduction in depth-scan frames with coded apertures, and tenfold detector improvement. Combined estimates are about 900 times faster for most measurements and up to 45,000 for some. Detector purchases were removed from the project scope. As-built spot sizes remain unpublished.
quantitative: In the 324-bunch brightness-mode design, horizontal electron-beam width changes from 280 to 14.7 µm and vertical width from 10 to 3.2 µm. These are root-mean-square widths.

The 3DMN design section uses a brightness gain of about 100. Its phrase about spot size and intensity improving linearly with brightness needs qualification. For fixed optics, flux density scales with brightness; spot size depends on source size and demagnification. Final-design Table 1.1 gives about 540 times greater brightness at 20 keV for an undulator optimized at that energy.

Pre-upgrade specifications give a 300 × 300 nm spot, or ranges of 300 to 500 nm horizontally and 300 to 700 nm vertically. At 14 keV, design spots are 103 × 68 nm at the micro station and 37 × 37 nm at the nano station. The tabulated widths are approximately full widths at half maximum; corresponding root-mean-square widths are about 50 × 35 and 19 × 19 nm.

Pink-beam sample flux changes from about 10¹¹ photons/s before the upgrade to a design 10¹⁴ photons/s. Monochromatic flux changes from about 10⁹ to 10¹¹ photons/s in the directory or 10¹² in the preliminary design.
The old mirrors required an opening about 60 × 60 µm for a 500 nm focus. Fully illuminated new mirrors give an estimated ninefold flux increase at the same or smaller spot size.
The preliminary design estimates about 900 times faster acquisition for most experiments, 4,500 for many and up to 45,000 for some.

A coded-aperture depth scan covers about 120 µm, eight 15 µm bits, compared with a 600 µm wire scan in 1 µm steps. This requires about five times fewer frames with lower noise. The preliminary-design target is 400 images rather than 2,000 per depth scan.
Projected annual raw data is about 2.8 PB, compared with about 400 TB at pre-upgrade 34-ID-E.

The derived horizontal coherent fraction at 14 keV increases from about 0.2% to 9%. This estimate uses Gaussian source sizes and divergences from final-design Table 1.1, plus single-electron photon contributions for a 2.1 m undulator.

techniques.name: Polychromatic Laue microdiffraction and nanodiffraction
techniques.text: Laue diffraction uses many X-ray energies simultaneously with a stationary sample. The mirror-filtered spectrum is called pink beam. Each set of crystal planes diffracts the wavelength satisfying Bragg's law for its spacing and angle. Spot directions determine grain orientation and deviatoric strain, the five components that change crystal shape. Without spot wavelengths, the overall expansion or contraction remains unknown. Typical strain precision is about 10⁻⁴, reaching about 2 × 10⁻⁵ under favourable conditions. Sample scanning gives two-dimensional maps; aperture scanning adds depth. Most useful signal on the upper detector is from 12 to 17 keV.

techniques.name: Differential-aperture X-ray microscopy with a wire
techniques.text: Differential-aperture X-ray microscopy, DAXM, separates diffraction from different depths. A platinum wire about 50 to 100 µm thick is scanned in roughly 1 µm steps within a millimetre of the surface. As its edge blocks a detector pixel, the corresponding ray path is determined. Its intersection with the incident beam locates the scattering depth. Typical depth resolution along the beam is 0.5 to 1 µm. Larson, Yang, Ice, Budai and Tischler introduced the method at the APS in Nature in 2002. It became a principal method at 34-ID-E.

techniques.name: Coded-aperture depth-resolved Laue diffraction
techniques.text: A patterned gold mask replaces the wire in coded-aperture Laue diffraction. Its 256-bit de Bruijn sequence contains each eight-bit subsequence once. The sequence of blocked and transmitted intensity during motion identifies the mask position and scattering depth. Eight bits of 15 µm require about 120 µm of scan, compared with about 600 µm for a wire. About five times fewer frames are needed, with lower noise. Reconstruction uses a search followed by a least-squares fit. The method was demonstrated at 34-ID-E before the upgrade and published during 2022 to 2025. It is expected to become standard as reconstruction software matures.

techniques.name: Monochromatic energy-scan micro/nano-diffraction
techniques.text: Two silicon crystals select a narrow energy band, about one part in 10,000. The energy is scanned until a selected indexed Laue reflection occurs. Its wavelength determines the absolute crystal-plane spacing, which is absent from a multi-energy pattern. The resulting overall expansion or contraction completes the six-component strain tensor. Combined with wire scanning, energy scans resolve lattice spacing by depth. Horizontal reflection is less efficient for horizontally polarized incident light. Estimated polarization losses grow from about 5 to 10% at 12 keV to roughly 25 to 50% at 5.3 keV.

techniques.name: Bragg coherent diffraction imaging on Laue-indexed grains
techniques.text: Bragg coherent diffraction imaging reconstructs a grain's shape and internal strain from intensity fringes around a reflection. Laue indexing first determines its orientation, from which the energy for a selected reflection is calculated. A coherent single-energy beam and a detector about 2 to 3 m away are then used. Energy scans replace sample rotation. The increased coherent fraction supports this method. The design includes it only at the micro station.

techniques.name: Scanning X-ray fluorescence
techniques.text: X-ray fluorescence has energies characteristic of the emitting elements. An energy-resolving silicon drift detector beside the sample records elemental maps. At 3DMN these measurements mainly locate features before diffraction mapping. The preliminary design preferred a 1 mm thick Vortex-class sensor for higher-energy fluorescence lines.

scienceCases.title: Hidden stresses inside dislocation cells of deformed metals
scienceCases.text: Deformation produces dislocations, line defects in atomic order. In copper, these defects form walls that divide grains into cells. Levine and colleagues measured large, widely distributed elastic strain cell by cell at the APS in 2006. Later measurements found opposite strain in walls and interiors, consistent with Mughrabi's composite model. The 3DMN design targets roughly 100 nm three-dimensional pixels to resolve strain within a wall. A 2026 study used pre-upgrade wire scans of a stainless-steel grain stretched by 2%, with 0.5 µm depth resolution. Unsupervised machine learning identified cell structures and their strain.

scienceCases.title: The strain field of a single dislocation
scienceCases.text: A dislocation distorts the surrounding crystal. Hofmann and colleagues mapped rotation and strain around one dislocation at 34-ID-E in 2013. The sample was a freestanding GaAs/In₀.₂Ga₀.₈As/GaAs membrane. Measurements agreed with elasticity calculations that include direction-dependent stiffness. Extending this measurement to a dislocation buried in bulk material requires a beam below 100 nm, a stated 3DMN design objective.

scienceCases.title: 3D-printed alloys
scienceCases.text: Solidification during metal 3D printing produces branched dendrites and composition changes over hundreds of nanometres. In nickel superalloys such as IN625 and IN718, primary arms are about 1 µm apart and secondary arms about 300 nm apart. Alloying elements segregate on these scales. The pre-upgrade beam averaged over this structure. A probe below 200 nm with energy scans is intended to determine all six strain components within it.

scienceCases.title: Materials at terapascal pressure
scienceCases.text: Compression between diamond tips to millions of atmospheres leaves samples only a few micrometres wide. Nanofabricated tips reduce sample dimensions toward 100 nm. The science case includes hydrogen phases III to V with 1 to 3 µm samples, and terapascal diffraction at about ten million atmospheres. These measurements require a beam near 50 nm and roughly a hundredfold brightness increase. The micro station's working distance provides space for pressure cells.

scienceCases.title: Strain engineering in transistors and oxide devices
scienceCases.text: Strain changes electron mobility in silicon. Measurements in finished devices are proposed for strain gradients at edges and interfaces in silicon-on-insulator and complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor structures with features below 32 nm. Other proposals concern domain switching under electric fields and temperature changes. Ferroelectrics have reversible electric polarization. Multiferroics combine electric polarization with magnetism. Relevant domain structures include stripes, toroids and bubbles. The preliminary design cites IBM on the industrial need for smaller probes.

scienceCases.title: Coherent imaging after Laue indexing
scienceCases.text: Laue indexing determines grain positions and orientations in a polycrystal. A selected grain or precipitate is then measured with coherent single-energy diffraction for three-dimensional reconstruction. In the Inconel 617 design example, indexing determines the energy and direction of a reflection from a carbide precipitate at a junction of three grains. A detector 2 to 3 m away records coherent scattering. Related work was demonstrated at 34-ID-C in 2020 and on tungsten specimens cut by focused ion beam to contain selected dislocations.

scienceCases.title: Coded apertures for fast 3D Laue
scienceCases.text: An APS team demonstrated coded-aperture depth reconstruction before the upgrade on a 75 µm nickel foil. A 7 to 30 keV beam was focused to about 300 nm, with the detector 510.9 mm above. The gold mask recovered the approximately 100 µm depth range with lower noise and five times fewer scan points than a 100 µm platinum wire. Later work added computational calibration of mask position. Design rules include bits at least as wide as the signal, aspect ratio near one, and scans of at least eight bits.

keyParameters.label: Energy range
keyParameters.value: 5.3 to 30 keV
keyParameters.note: The final design gives the shared ATOMIC beam-delivery range. The directory lists 5.5 to 30 keV; the former 34-ID-E range was 7 to 30 keV. Mirror critical angle limits the upper energy and monochromator geometry the lower energy.

keyParameters.label: Source
keyParameters.value: Planar hybrid PM undulator, 28 mm period, 2.1 m, upstream slot of canted straight, outboard branch
keyParameters.note: Final-design Table 4.62 gives 777 W through the 2 × 2 mm exit mask at 30 m for K = 2.459. IPAC'24 lists required K = 2.48 at the 8.5 mm minimum gap, first harmonic 3.0 keV and roughly 2.1 m canted magnetic length.

keyParameters.label: Canting
keyParameters.value: 1 mrad between upstream outboard 3DMN and downstream inboard ATOMIC
keyParameters.note: End canting magnets deflect 0.5 mrad each, with a 1 mrad magnet between undulators.

keyParameters.label: Front end
keyParameters.value: Canted-undulator front end, CUFE, windowless, differential pump, 2 ×, 2 mm H × 2 mm V exit apertures 1 mrad apart at 25.4 m; 2 × 10 kW
keyParameters.note: The exit collimator at 26.1 m has two 5 × 5 mm openings.

keyParameters.label: First mirror, 34ID-MR-1
keyParameters.value: Flat, horizontally deflecting, 3.0 mrad, Si/Rh/Pt stripes, notched substrate, at 29.6 m
keyParameters.note: The silicon stripe absorbs up to about 189 W, or 0.48 W/mm², with 1 × 1 mm acceptance and the 9.1 keV third harmonic in Table 4.66. The 2017 plan proposed liquid-nitrogen-cooled mirrors. Final-design text omits deflection sense; the Fig. 4.59 schematic and preliminary-design text place 3DMN reflection outboard and ATOMIC inboard.

keyParameters.label: Monochromator, 34ID-MN-2
keyParameters.value: Horizontally deflecting Si(111) double-crystal, ≈1.1 mm offset, pink-beam bypass, heated 2nd crystal, ΔT ≈ 60 K, at 53.8 m
keyParameters.note: Si(111) is specified in the preliminary design and inferred from the 12.5° angle at 9.1 keV in final-design Table 4.67. Required acceptance is below 300 × 300 µm. A predecessor synthetic-channel-cut Si(111) device was installed at 34-ID-C before the upgrade, described by Pateras and colleagues in 2020. It covered 6 to 20 keV, with a 1 mm offset, air-bearing granite support, sideways pink-beam retraction and heated second crystal.

keyParameters.label: Energy resolution, mono
keyParameters.value: dE/E ≈ 10⁻⁴
keyParameters.note: Si(111) double bounce; same as pre-upgrade spec.

keyParameters.label: Micro-focus spot, design, 14 keV
keyParameters.value: 103 × 68 nm² (H × V) brightness mode; 91 × 100 nm² timing mode
keyParameters.note: These are final-design Table 4.64 ray traces near 60 m. The directory lists 0.15 × 0.15 µm; measured as-built width is unpublished. The table omits width definition. Fig. 4.61 gives root-mean-square widths near 50 × 35 nm at zero figure error, so the table values are approximately twice these, similar to full width at half maximum. The upgrade performance criteria were brightness and usable energy range, with focal width specified only for ISN. Reported compliance therefore does not verify the 3DMN focus.

keyParameters.label: Nano-focus spot, design, 14 keV
keyParameters.value: 37 × 37 nm² brightness mode; 38 × 37 nm² timing mode
keyParameters.note: The nano pair is near 65.5 m. Installation and commissioning are undocumented as of October 2026. Fig. 4.61 gives root-mean-square widths near 19 × 19 nm.

keyParameters.label: Flux on sample, design
keyParameters.value: Micro 4.9 × 10¹², nano 4.9 × 10¹¹ ph/s/0.1%BW at 14 keV; pink ≈10¹⁴ ph/s; mono ≈10¹¹–10¹² ph/s
keyParameters.note: Pink and monochromatic totals are from the preliminary design and directory. The directory gives 10¹⁴ pink photons/s and 10¹¹ monochromatic photons/s at 15 keV.

keyParameters.label: KB mirrors
keyParameters.value: Two fixed-figure, prefigured elliptical cylinder Pt-coated KB pairs at 3.0 mrad; micro at ≈60 m, nano at ≈65.5 m
keyParameters.note: To limit spot growth below 10%, root-mean-square figure errors must be below 0.75 nm horizontally and 0.5 nm vertically at the micro station, or 0.5 and 0.4 nm at the nano station.

keyParameters.label: Working distance
keyParameters.value: ≥ 50 mm, micro, design goal; ≈30 mm, nano
keyParameters.note: Working distances are 2017 design values. That design gives horizontal and vertical focal lengths 70 and 142 mm for a station at 62 m, and 55 and 120 mm for one at 66 m. As-built geometry may differ.

keyParameters.label: Detector geometry, reference: pre-upgrade 34-ID-E
keyParameters.value: PerkinElmer XRD1621, 2048 × 2048, 200 µm pixels, 409.6 mm square ≈511 to 513 mm above sample in 90° reflection geometry; two 1024 × 1024, 204.8 mm PE side panels ≈0.40 m perpendicular distance, ≈0.43 m to panel centre, outboard and inboard
keyParameters.note: The pre-upgrade top distance is 510.9 mm in Gursoy and colleagues, 2022, and about 511 mm in Das and colleagues, 2018. Lauelab geometry files dated 2022-03-29 and 2023-04-06 identify top PE1621 723-3335 near 513 mm and side PE0822 883-4841/4843 near 400 mm perpendicular distance, or 428 mm to the centre. Model names differ across sources. The 2024 computing strategy lists PE XRD 1620 AN and two PE XRD 0820 AN panels; the Instruments page also lists XRD 0820 AN. Planned replacements were a Pilatus 6M-class top and two 1 to 2 megapixel side panels. The computing strategy estimates growth from 6 to 10 megapixels per point with two 2-megapixel sides. Purchases were removed from the upgrade scope. The August 2026 ModSim talk proposed a tenfold faster detector without naming it and mentioned wire reconstruction with Eiger. Current detectors remain unknown.

keyParameters.label: Sample geometry
keyParameters.value: Sample surface inclined 45° to the incident beam; wire moves along H = (Y+Z)/√2
keyParameters.note: 34-ID-E coordinates: X horizontal outboard, Y up, Z along beam; 45° reflection geometry.

keyParameters.label: Depth-resolving aperture
keyParameters.value: Platinum wire 0.2 to 1 mm above the sample. Historical diameter about 50 µm; 2022 tests 100 µm; geometry files 101.5 µm. Alternative gold mask has 4.6 µm thickness and 7.5/15 µm bits in a 256-bit de Bruijn sequence.
keyParameters.note: The CCD-era End near focus photo, before 2009, depicts an approximately 50 µm platinum wire about 200 µm above the sample.

keyParameters.label: Depth resolution
keyParameters.value: ≈0.5 to 1 µm along the beam, DAXM, pre-upgrade
keyParameters.note: SharafEldin and colleagues, 2026, report 0.5 µm depth resolution. Coded-aperture demonstrations use 1 µm steps. The new-beam goal is about 100 nm, requiring roughly five times more frames without coded apertures.

keyParameters.label: Strain resolution
keyParameters.value: ≈10⁻⁴ in deviatoric strain, best ≈2 × 10⁻⁵
keyParameters.note: The preliminary-design target is dd/d = 10⁻⁴. A 1999 APS report gives better than 2 × 10⁻⁵ under favourable conditions. White-beam indexing determines deviatoric strain; one monochromatic energy measurement completes the tensor. At about 511 mm, a 200 µm pixel subtends 3.9 × 10⁻⁴ rad in 2θ, or about 2 × 10⁻⁴ in plane-normal direction and dd/d at 2θ = 90°. Precision at 10⁻⁴ or below requires subpixel fitting across reflections. The design rule of one pixel near 10⁻⁴ would require roughly 1 m distance.

keyParameters.label: Thermal stability requirement
keyParameters.value: Hutch 0.03 to 0.05 °C; nano-instrument enclosure ≤ 0.02 °C
keyParameters.note: The preliminary design calculates 100 nm expansion for a 100 mm aluminium part during a 0.04 °C change.

keyParameters.label: Distances
keyParameters.value: Micro instrument 60.0 m, nano instrument 65.5 m, pink beam stop 66.9 m from source
keyParameters.note: FDR Table 4.63.

keyParameters.label: Analysis software
keyParameters.value: LaueGo on Igor Pro for wire reconstruction, peak search, euler indexing and strain refinement. Lauelab uses Python, C and CUDA, in alpha development from 2023. Laue-portal is a Dash web workflow with Polaris computing.
keyParameters.note: J. Z. Tischler wrote LaueGo. Lauelab reproduces its numerical methods for wire reconstruction and indexing. Laue-portal supplies a web workflow, with cold for coded-mask decoding. Fifty Polaris nodes processed February and April 2023 coded scans of 6 to 12 h duration and returned results 12 to 15 minutes behind collection. This appears in the SC'23 Workshops and XLOOP 2023 paper. Liu and Ice, 2014, provide background.

insertionDevices.name: Upstream 3DMN undulator U28
insertionDevices.type: Planar hybrid permanent-magnet undulator. The new structure uses NdFeB magnets with heavy-rare-earth grain-boundary diffusion for increased coercivity and vanadium-permendur poles.
insertionDevices.notes: The upstream 34-ID device supplies the outboard branch. The final-design maximum-power calculation uses K = 2.459, giving 777 W through a 2 × 2 mm mask at 30 m. IPAC'24 gives required K = 2.48 at the 8.5 mm minimum gap and first harmonic near 3.0 keV. At 6 GeV, E1 = 12.2/(1+K²/2) keV, giving about 3.0 keV at K = 2.459 and third harmonic 9.1 keV in Table 4.66. Higher energies use odd harmonics. Maximum gap taper is 5 mm, requested in the preliminary design for broadening the Laue spectrum. The final-design 2.1 m magnetic length is consistent with IPAC'24 canted-device length, compared with about 2.4 m full length. The ATOMIC directory's 2.3 m revolver value differs.

insertionDevices.name: Downstream ATOMIC revolver undulator U25/U21
insertionDevices.type: Planar hybrid permanent-magnet revolver undulator with 25 and 21 mm structures
insertionDevices.notes: The downstream device supplies inboard ATOMIC at 34-ID-F. Maximum power through the 2 × 2 mm mask at 30 m is 763 W at K = 1.939 or 738 W at K = 1.305. It shares the straight section, canting magnets and front end with 3DMN.

source.canting: The angle between devices is 1.0 mrad. End magnets each deflect 0.5 mrad, with a 1 mrad magnet between the devices. Upstream 3DMN is outboard; downstream ATOMIC is inboard. From the 2011 canting upgrade until the ring upgrade, the assignment was reversed. Then 34-ID-E used the downstream inboard beam and 34-ID-C the outboard beam.
source.frontEnd: The canted-undulator front end has limits of two 10 kW beams and 280 kW/mrad² peak density. Differential pumping provides a windowless exit. Components include clearing magnet, low-power photon shutter, burn-through mask, GRID fluorescence monitor XBPM1, exit-mask monitor XBPM2, and photon and safety shutters. At 25.4 m, two 2 × 2 mm exit openings are separated by 1 mrad. At 26.1 m, the tungsten collimator has two 5 × 5 mm openings.
source.sourceSizeAndDivergence: Final-design Table 1.1 gives root-mean-square electron-beam widths and divergences. In brightness mode with 324 bunches and 42 pm emittance, horizontal and vertical widths are 14.7 and 3.2 µm; divergences are 2.8 and 1.3 µrad. Timing mode with 48 bunches and 32 pm gives 12.9 and 8.8 µm, with 2.5 and 3.7 µrad. Pre-upgrade values are 280 and 10 µm, with 11.6 and 3.4 µrad. For a 2.1 m device at 14 keV, derived photon contributions are about 1.5 µm and 4.6 µrad, from σr = √(2·λ·L)/(4·π) and σr' = √(λ/(2L)). The combined photon source is about 14.8 × 3.6 µm and 5.4 × 4.8 µrad root-mean-square. Source points are about 1 m from the straight centre, where beta functions differ slightly.

branches.name: 3DMN outboard canted branch
branches.description: The upstream U28 supplies the outboard branch through the shared front end. Mirror MR-1 in A precedes masks in B, monitoring and slits in C, the small-offset crystal monochromator with pink bypass, and shutter. The micro instrument is near 60 m in E and planned nano instrument near 65.5 m, with installation unconfirmed. The stop is at 66.9 m.

branches.name: Partner ATOMIC inboard branch
branches.description: The downstream U25/U21 revolver supplies inboard ATOMIC. Mirror MR-2 precedes its monochromator and first mirror pair in C. Shielded transport extends through E from 55.1 to 67.5 m. The final mirrors and coherent-imaging instrument occupy F near 68 to 70 m, with a stop at 78.7 m. ATOMIC has a separate exhibit.

components.name: 3DMN undulator, 28 mm period, upstream
components.distanceNote: Distances in this exhibit are measured, as in FDR Table 4.63, from the centre of the 34-ID straight, the canting-magnet position. The U28 is the upstream device; its centre is placed ≈1.2 m upstream, approximate: two 2.1 m devices plus a central canting magnet in the ≈4.8 m straight.
components.text: This 2.1 m undulator has alternating permanent magnets with a 28 mm period. Their fields bend 6 GeV electron trajectories; radiation from successive bends combines into a narrow beam. Closing the gap strengthens the field and lowers the harmonic energies. At the 8.5 mm minimum gap, the first harmonic is near 3.0 keV. Higher odd harmonics occur at 3, 5, 7 and further odd multiples. A gap taper up to 5 mm broadens the harmonics for a smoother Laue spectrum. Use of taper after the upgrade is undocumented.

components.name: Canting magnets, 0.5, 1.0 and 0.5 mrad
components.distanceNote: The central magnet defines distance zero. The end magnets each deflect 0.5 mrad and are placed approximately 2.4 m either side of the centre.
components.text: Three magnets change the electron direction by 1 mrad, about 0.06°, between the undulators. Their diverging X-ray beams supply 3DMN and ATOMIC from one straight section. The upstream device supplies outboard 3DMN, away from the ring. Before the upgrade, 34-ID-E used the inboard beam.

components.name: Partner ATOMIC downstream revolver undulator, U25/U21
components.distanceNote: Downstream device of the same straight, centre ≈+1.2 m from the straight centre, approx..
components.text: The downstream revolver undulator supplies ATOMIC for coherent imaging of strain in nanocrystals. Two magnet structures with 25 and 21 mm periods share a rotating support. The selected period depends on measurement energy. This source is included to explain the shared straight section; it does not supply 3DMN.

components.name: Canted-undulator front end, CUFE
components.distanceNote: The front end extends roughly 14 to 25 m within the shielding tunnel. The upstream GRID mask position is documented at 19.4 m. Other positions are approximate and absent from the final design.
components.text: The front end connects the accelerator to the beamlines inside the concrete tunnel. Masks absorb unwanted power, fluorescence monitors measure beam position, and photon and safety shutters block beam for access. The power limit is 10 kW for each of two beams. Differential pumping separates the vacuums without a window, preserving the coherent wavefront.

specs.XBPM: GRID XBPM1 + XBPM2 in exit mask
specs.elements: clearing magnet, low-power photon shutter, burn-through fixed mask, GRID XBPM1, photon shutter 2, safety shutters

components.name: Front-end exit mask, two 2 × 2 mm² apertures
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63.
components.text: This metal block has two 2 mm square openings on axes separated by 1 mrad. Each transmits the central portion of one beam while the surrounding block absorbs the rest. Beam-position monitor XBPM2 is integrated into it.

components.name: Front-end exit collimator
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63.
components.text: This tungsten block has a 5 mm square opening for each beam. It confines bremsstrahlung, high-energy radiation from interactions of stored electrons with residual gas. The upgrade reduced the opening for small monochromator offsets such as 3DMN's roughly 1 mm offset.

components.name: White-beam slits, inboard, ATOMIC 34ID-SL-1
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63.
components.text: Tungsten-edged jaws limit the ATOMIC white beam, containing the full undulator spectrum. Each branch has separate slits; these are upstream of the 3DMN pair.

components.name: White-beam slits, outboard, 3DMN 34ID-SL-2
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63.
components.text: Water-cooled tungsten-edged jaws limit the 3DMN white beam before the mirror. Reducing the opening lowers absorbed heat. Required illumination is about 1 × 1 mm at the mirror and less than 0.3 × 0.3 mm at the monochromator.

specs.acceptance needed: ≈1 × 1 mm² at mirror, < 300 × 300 µm² at mono

components.name: Tungsten bremsstrahlung collimator 34ID-BC-1
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63.
components.text: This tungsten collimator has openings for both X-ray beams. It confines stray bremsstrahlung from the accelerator.

components.name: Lead bremsstrahlung collimator 34ID-BC-2
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63.
components.text: A lead collimator follows the tungsten block for additional shielding against high-energy accelerator radiation. Both X-ray beams pass through openings.

components.name: Outboard horizontal deflecting mirror 34ID-MR-1, 3DMN
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63.
components.text: The flat silicon mirror reflects the 3DMN beam outboard at a 3 mrad grazing angle, or 0.17°. Higher-energy X-rays are not reflected, reducing downstream heat. Silicon, rhodium and platinum stripes give estimated cutoffs near 10, 22 and 28 keV. A substrate notch reduces thermal deformation about tenfold. Absorbed power reaches 189 W.

specs.cooling: notch design, coolant not stated in FDR; PDR proposed LN₂
specs.deflection direction: outboard, PDR text; FDR Fig. 4.59 schematic
specs.estimated cutoffs at 3 mrad: Si ≈10, Rh ≈22, Pt ≈28 keV, some usable flux to 30 keV, PDR

components.name: Secondary bremsstrahlung collimator 34ID-SC-1
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63.
components.text: This shielding block is after the mirror, where the reflected X-rays and straight-through bremsstrahlung follow different paths. It confines the straight-through radiation.

components.name: Inboard horizontal deflecting mirror 34ID-MR-2, ATOMIC
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63.
components.text: The ATOMIC mirror has silicon, rhodium and platinum stripes at a 3 mrad grazing angle. Reflection is inboard toward the ring, opposite the 3DMN deflection. The beam paths are about 0.4 m apart in 34-ID-E.

specs.deflection direction: inboard, PDR text; FDR Fig. 4.59 schematic

components.name: Secondary bremsstrahlung collimator 34ID-SC-2
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63, branch not stated.
components.text: This collimator confines stray radiation continuing straight past the ATOMIC mirror. The reflected X-ray beam follows a separate path.

components.name: Diagnostic flag 34ID-BD-1
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63.
components.text: A fluorescent screen moves into the reflected beams for camera alignment measurements. It is after both mirrors and before the first-hutch exit.

components.name: Pink photon mask / white-beam stop 34ID-PM-1
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63.

components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63, inboard PM-2 at same position for ATOMIC.

components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63, ATOMIC BPM 49.7 m and slits 50.3 m precede it.

components.distanceNote: Final-design Table 4.63 places the pair at 52.0 m, while the text gives station C at 54 m. The discrepancy is unresolved.

components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63.

components.name: Small-offset horizontal double-crystal monochromator 34ID-MN-2, 3DMN
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63.
components.text: Two Si(111) crystals select energy by Bragg reflection over 5.3 to 30 keV with relative width about 10⁻⁴. The design permits retraction in seconds for pink beam, the configuration shown here. Horizontal reflections shift the beam sideways about 1.1 mm. Heating the second crystal by about 60 °C changes lattice spacing and exit angle to align the two modes. The calculated angle change is about 20 to 125 µrad depending on energy. Closing the full offset at the micro mirrors would require about 180 µrad. The operating alignment procedure is unconfirmed.

components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63, ATOMIC SH-1 at same position.

components.name: ATOMIC shielded transport through 34-ID-E 34ID-ST-2
components.distanceNote: Spans 55.1 to 67.5 m, FDR Table 4.63. In FDR Fig. 4.58 it runs ≈0.4 m inboard of the 3DMN beam, approx. from figure.

components.name: Micro-focusing KB mirror pair, micro-diffraction instrument 34ID-BI-1
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63 / text: KB and instrument at 60 m, ray traces at '60 m'. The pair deflects both vertically, first mirror and horizontally, second mirror.
components.text: Two Kirkpatrick-Baez mirrors focus vertically and horizontally at 3 mrad grazing incidence. Focusing is independent of energy, so pink and monochromatic beam have the same nominal focus. At 14 keV, ray tracing gives 103 × 68 nm, approximately full widths at half maximum, with 4.9 × 10¹² photons/s in a 0.1% band. The platinum-coated surfaces require 0.5 to 0.75 nm root-mean-square shape accuracy. The directory lists 150 × 150 nm. As-built measurements are unpublished.

components.name: Micro station sample stage, 45° geometry
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. focus ≈0.1 m downstream of the 60.0 m KB position, PDR focal lengths f_v ≈142 mm, f_h ≈70 mm; not tabulated.
components.text: Motorized stages scan a sample tilted 45° through the beam in steps down to about 10 nm. An optical microscope views the surface normally. A working distance of at least 50 mm provides space for heaters, mechanical loading and diamond pressure cells.

components.name: Depth-profiling wire / knife-edge scanner, DAXM
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. at the micro sample; wire ≈0.2 to 1 mm above the sample surface.
components.text: A platinum wire about 50 to 100 µm thick is scanned 0.2 to 1 mm above the surface in roughly 1 µm steps. Blocking of a detector pixel determines a ray path from the wire edge to that pixel. Its intersection with the incident beam gives scattering depth. Scans take 50 to 2,000 frames per sample point with 0.5 to 1 µm resolution along the beam. The wire and gap are enlarged in the model.

components.name: Experimental coded gold aperture
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. replaces the wire at the micro sample, ≈0.84 to 1 mm above the surface, as in the 34-ID-E tests; drawn parked beside the wire.
components.text: The alternative coded mask has gold bars on a silicon-nitride membrane. Its 256-bit de Bruijn pattern contains each eight-bit subsequence once. A scan about 120 µm long determines diffraction depths with about one-fifth of the wire-scan frames. Gold thickness is about 4.6 µm, with nominal 7.5 µm bars and 15 µm gaps. The enlarged mask is shown parked beside the wire.

components.name: Main area detector above the sample, 90° reflection geometry
components.distanceNote: Along-beam position = micro sample, 60.1 m. Panel centre ≈0.513 m above the sample and ≈30 mm downstream of it, face horizontal, pre-upgrade lauelab geometry file geoN_2023-04-06; 510.9 mm in Gursoy et al. 2022.
components.text: The main detector faces downward about half a metre above the sample. Laue spot directions determine grain orientation and strain. The pre-upgrade PerkinElmer panel had 2048 × 2048 pixels of 200 µm. At that distance, a pixel corresponds to about 2 × 10⁻⁴ in lattice spacing, so 10⁻⁴ strain precision requires subpixel fitting. A Pilatus 6M-class detector was specified, but its purchase was removed from the upgrade scope. The current detector is undocumented. Model rays are calculated for two nickel grains and coloured by photon energy.

components.name: Two side area detectors
components.distanceNote: The side panel centres are about 0.14 m upstream of the micro sample. Each is tilted 45° about the beam, with its normal upward and outboard or inboard. Perpendicular distance is about 0.40 m and centre distance about 0.43 m. These positions follow pre-upgrade lauelab file geoN_2023-04-06, with Yellow outboard and Purple inboard.
components.text: Two side detectors record reflections outside the main panel's acceptance, improving orientation and strain measurements, especially shear. Each is about 0.4 m from the sample. The pre-upgrade 1024 × 1024 PerkinElmer panels were called Yellow outboard and Purple inboard. The design specifies 1 to 2 megapixels per panel.

specs.pre-upgrade: Two PerkinElmer 1024 × 1024 panels, named XRD 0820 AN or PE0822 in different sources

components.name: Fluorescence detector, SDD
components.distanceNote: Along-beam position ≈ micro sample; snout a few cm from the sample, approx..
components.text: A silicon drift detector a few centimetres from the sample records characteristic elemental fluorescence. Elemental maps locate features for subsequent diffraction. The preliminary design preferred a 1 mm thick sensor for higher-energy emission lines.

components.name: Far-field coherent, BCDI detector, movable
components.distanceNote: The preliminary design places the far detector about 2 to 3 m from the micro sample. One example uses 3.3 m at 12 keV for 1.5 µm particles and 75 µm pixels. The exhibit position is illustrative, about 2.2 m upward and outboard at 2θ near 72°, as for Ni 400 at 12 keV. This path exits through the 45° sample surface and clears the gantry and side panels. Its along-beam coordinate is about 60.8 m.
components.text: A movable detector about 2 to 3 m from the sample records coherent intensity fringes around a selected Bragg reflection. Computation reconstructs a grain's three-dimensional shape and strain from these measurements. Energy scans traverse the reflection while the sample remains stationary. This design mode is only for the micro station. The model position is illustrative.

components.name: Nano-diffraction thermal enclosure
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. upstream wall of a ≈2.8 to 3 m enclosure around the 65.5 m instrument, 3000 mm dimension in FDR Fig. 4.67; ≈2.5 m footprint at ≈64.3 to 66.8 m in Fig. 4.58.
components.text: The nano instrument is designed within a clear-walled enclosure about 3 m long. A 100 mm aluminium part expands about 100 nm during a 0.04 °C temperature change, exceeding the 40 nm spot. The local stability requirement is 0.02 °C, compared with 0.03 to 0.05 °C for the hutch. Electronics are outside the enclosure and the instrument rests on a stable table. The old steel-supported table had roughly 50 nm vibration.

components.name: Nano-focusing KB mirror pair, nano-diffraction instrument 34ID-BI-2
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63 / text: 65.5 m, ray traces at '65 m'. The pair deflects both vertically, first mirror and horizontally, second mirror.
components.text: The design focal width for the shorter-focus mirror pair at 65.5 m is about 40 nm. At 14 keV, ray tracing gives 37 × 37 nm with 4.9 × 10¹¹ photons/s in a 0.1% band, ten times less flux than the micro station. Platinum-coated surface accuracy must be 0.4 to 0.5 nm root-mean-square. Working distance is about 30 mm. Installation and commissioning remain undocumented as of October 2026.

components.name: Nano station sample stage with interferometric nanopositioners
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. a few cm downstream of the nano KB.
components.text: Interferometers measure sample-stage position during scanning through the approximately 40 nm focus. The preliminary design specifies about 5 nm positioning accuracy. The stage rests on a stable optical table inside the thermal enclosure.

components.name: Nano station precision knife-edge / wire scanner
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. just above the sample.
components.text: A knife edge or wire is scanned just above the nano sample with about 5 nm precision. Blocking at known positions separates diffraction from different depths, as at the micro station.

components.name: Nano station flat-panel detectors
components.distanceNote: Above/around the sample, approx..
components.text: Detectors above and beside the nano sample record Laue patterns. The diffracted intensity decreases with illuminated depth-slice thickness, requiring low noise. The design includes an upper panel, two side panels and a forward panel. Installed detectors are unknown.

components.name: Partner ATOMIC coherent-imaging endstation, 34ID-BI-3
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.63, KB2 at 68.1 m; beam stop 78.7 m.

instruments.name: 3D microdiffraction instrument, 34ID-BI-1
instruments.text: The micro station is near 60 m. Kirkpatrick-Baez mirrors focus pink or single-energy X-rays on a sample tilted 45°. The design spot is 103 × 68 nm at 14 keV; the directory lists 150 × 150 nm. A wire or coded gold mask separates diffraction by depth. Upper and side detectors record Laue spots, and a distant detector is specified for coherent imaging. Each scan point requires 50 to 2,000 frames. Software reconstructs depth, indexes reflections and calculates orientation and deviatoric strain. Energy scans determine absolute strain. A working distance of at least 50 mm accommodates heaters, loading equipment, diamond cells and an in situ nanoindenter.
detectors: Large area detector above the sample in 90° reflection geometry, pre-upgrade PerkinElmer XRD1621, 2048 × 2048, at ≈511 mm; design Pilatus 6M class.
Two side area detectors, pre-upgrade PerkinElmer 1024 × 1024 panels, XRD 0820 AN / 'PE0822'; design 1 to 2 Mpixel.
Silicon drift fluorescence detector, Vortex class.
Forward-scattering medium area detector on a horizontal motion, PDR; the pre-upgrade directory lists a Mar 165 CCD for forward scattering.
Movable far-field small-pixel detector at ≈2 to 3 m for Bragg coherent imaging.
Ion chambers before and after the KB mirrors, pre-upgrade I_start, I_middle, I_final.
sampleEnvironments: Small environmental chambers within the ≥ 50 mm working distance, PDR.
Heating and cooling, electric and magnetic fields, and mechanical loading, FDR science scope.
In situ nanoindenter, NIST-funded development, PDR.

instruments.name: 3D nanodiffraction instrument, 34ID-BI-2
instruments.text: The nano station at 65.5 m targets about 40 nm. Its design specifies a clear-walled enclosure with 0.02 °C thermal stability, a stable table and interferometric sample positioning accurate to about 5 nm. Low-noise detectors are needed for the small diffracting volume in each depth slice. The approximately 30 mm working distance limits sample environments to compact equipment. Construction and commissioning remain undocumented as of October 2026.
detectors: Flat-panel or photon-counting area detectors above and beside the sample, design.
sampleEnvironments: The reduced working distance, ≈30 mm, PDR limits environments to compact stages.

geometryNotes:
The 34-ID pair has a 1 mrad angle between sources. The upstream undulator supplies the outboard 3DMN beam; the downstream undulator supplies inboard ATOMIC. This reverses the pre-upgrade assignment, when 34-ID-E used the inboard beam.

Each branch has a flat mirror in 34-ID-A at 3.0 mrad grazing incidence, giving 6 mrad deflection. The 3DMN mirror is at 29.6 m, ATOMIC's at 31.3 m. Preliminary-design text and final-design Fig. 4.59 place the deflections outboard and inboard respectively. At the preliminary-design 2.5 mrad incidence, beam separation was about 11 mrad. Final-design Fig. 4.58 depicts about 0.4 m between the 3DMN beam and ATOMIC pipe in 34-ID-E. This is consistent with roughly 58 mm source-angle separation plus 6 mrad × 28 m deflection on each side. Both small-offset horizontal crystal monochromators are in 34-ID-C and displace the beam sideways by about 1.1 mm.

The hutches occupy the existing sector-34 experiment floor. Final-design plan-scaled extents are A from about 24.4 to 36.0 m, shielded transport from 36.0 to 42.5 m, B from 42.3 to 47.8 m, C from 47.8 to 55.0 m, E from 55.0 to 67.5 m with stepped width, and F from 67.5 to 79.8 m.

The 3DMN pink-beam stop is at 66.9 m in E. ATOMIC continues through E in shielded transport from 55.1 to 67.5 m, entering F.

At the 3DMN sample, the beam direction is +Z. The surface is tilted 45°, with its normal upward and upstream. The upper detector is about 0.5 m above, with its centre at 2θ near 90°. Side panels are outboard and inboard, slightly upstream and raised, about 0.4 m away perpendicularly or 0.43 m to their centres. The wire moves parallel to the surface along H = (Y+Z)/√2, about 0.2 to 1 mm above it. The vertical focusing mirror is first. The horizontal mirror is about 6 to 7 cm from the micro focus, based on preliminary-design focal lengths.

The coordinates are X outboard toward the doors, Y upward and Z downstream. The nano station occupies a roughly 3 m glass thermal enclosure on a stable table downstream in E.

Exhibit distances refer to the straight-section centre, with the 28 mm-period undulator near −1.2 m and the ATOMIC revolver near +1.2 m. Enclosure outlines and offsets are scaled from final-design Fig. 4.58. The source angle and opposing mirror deflections give about 0.4 m beam separation in E. The wire, coded mask, sample gap and monochromator offset are enlarged for visibility. Their physical sizes are stated in the text.

interactiveIdeas.title: Laue diffraction and energy selection
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors rotate a crystal, such as face-centred-cubic nickel. A detector 0.5 m above records many spots under pink illumination. With monochromatic illumination, most reflections are absent. An energy scan brings a selected reflection into diffraction and determines its wavelength.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Multi-energy illumination records reflections from differently oriented grains without rotating the sample. Spot directions determine orientation. A narrow-band energy measurement supplies absolute lattice spacing.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Use Bragg's law λ = 2 d sinθ and E[keV] = 12.398/λ[Å]. For plane normal n, k_out = k_in − 2(k_in·n)n. A reflection occurs if E_hkl = 12.398/(2 d_hkl sinθ) falls within the approximately 5 to 30 keV mirror-filtered band. Most upper-panel signal is from 12 to 17 keV. Harmonics nh, nk, nl share a pixel. At the top centre, 2θ = 90° and E = 12.398/(√2 d). Intensity depends on |F_hkl|², spectrum and Lorentz and polarization factors. U28 first harmonic is E1 = 12.2/(1+K²/2) keV. Taper broadens its uneven harmonic spectrum.

interactiveIdeas.title: Depth reconstruction with a wire
interactiveIdeas.concept: Three depths within a sample tilted 45° contribute diffraction to an upper detector. Visitors scan a wire across the outgoing rays. Intensity differences identify blocking positions. Rays traced from the pixels past the edge intersect the incident beam at their scattering depths.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Wire geometry determines scattering depth. Aperture position, detector pixels and scan step limit depth resolution, requiring many frames.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Depth along the beam is the intersection with a ray from a detector pixel tangent to the wire. Lauelab uses tanφ = (tanφ0 ∓ tandφ)/(1 ± tanφ0 tandφ), with tandφ = a/√(r² − a²). For a pixel directly above, motion dH along H = (Y+Z)/√2 changes beam depth by dH/√2 × L/(L−h), about 0.71 dH. Wire height h is about 0.2 to 1 mm and detector distance L about 510 mm. Pixel blur p·h/L is about 0.08 to 0.4 µm for 200 µm pixels. Normal depth below the surface is beam depth times sin45°. The leading edge removes intensity and the trailing edge restores it, giving opposite differences. Platinum diameter is 50 to 100 µm; step is about 1 µm. Angular acceptance sets a scan length of hundreds of micrometres.

interactiveIdeas.title: Depth reconstruction with a coded mask
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors replace the wire with a gold de Bruijn mask. Blocked and transmitted intensity at each pixel forms a sequence during motion. A search for its unique match identifies mask position and depth. The display compares frame counts for wire and mask reconstruction of the same volume.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Each eight-bit window is unique. This reduces the required scan length. Bit size, absorption thickness and noise constrain decoding.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Use an order-eight binary de Bruijn sequence with 256 bits and unique eight-bit subsequences. Gold bits are nominally 7.5 µm wide for binary one; openings are 15 µm for zero. At least 120 µm scan is required, versus roughly 600 µm for a wire. Measurement is d = A_p s with a Toeplitz coding matrix. Reconstruction uses exhaustive offset search and non-negative least squares. A 4.6 µm gold layer transmits significant flux at 20 to 30 keV. Contrast decreases with energy and obliquity up to about 20° on a detector 51 cm away. Signals wider than a bit blur the sequence.

interactiveIdeas.title: Source size, aperture and focal width
interactiveIdeas.concept: A split view compares old electron-beam widths of 280 × 10 µm with upgraded widths of 14.7 × 3.2 µm, both root-mean-square. The same mirror pair is used. Controls change source distance, focal distance, opening and surface error. The display calculates spot width and flux.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: The focus contains a demagnified source image plus diffraction and surface-error contributions. A smaller source and more accurate mirrors increase usable flux at a small focus.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Add focal contributions in quadrature. Source-image full width at half maximum is 2.355 σ_src q/p. Diffraction width is about 0.88 λq/D, equivalent to 0.44 λ/NA with NA = D/(2q). Slope-error width is about 2 × 2.355 × σ_slope × q. Demagnification is roughly 60 m divided by 0.07 to 0.15 m, or 400 to 900. Horizontal source full width is about 35 µm upgraded and 660 µm old. Final-design anchors at 14 keV are 103 × 68 nm micro and 37 × 37 nm nano, with corresponding root-mean-square values near 50 × 35 and 19 × 19 nm. Root-mean-square figure tolerance is 0.4 to 0.75 nm for below 10% degradation. Source displacement dx moves the focus by dx q/p. Beam-angle error dψ at the mirror moves it about dψ q.

interactiveIdeas.title: Alignment of pink and monochromatic beam
interactiveIdeas.concept: An animation inserts or retracts the small-offset monochromator. Heating the second crystal changes its lattice spacing and outgoing beam angle. The display compares the two spots at the sample.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Thermal expansion changes Bragg angle and exit direction. Pink and narrow-band measurements require illumination of the same submicrometre sample volume.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Si(111) spacing is 3.1356 Å. Bragg angles range from 21.9° at 5.3 keV to 3.8° at 30 keV. With expansion coefficient α ≈ 2.6 × 10⁻⁶/K, heating changes spacing by αΔT and angle by Δθ = αΔT tanθB. Exit tilt is 2Δθ, about 125, 70, 45 and 21 µrad at 5.3, 9, 14 and 30 keV for 60 K. Closing 1.1 mm offset over about 6 m to the micro mirrors requires 180 µrad; over 11.7 m to nano mirrors requires 95 µrad. The preliminary-design kinematic polarization-loss estimates are about one-half at 5.3 keV, one-quarter at 8 keV and 10% at 12 keV. Perfect-crystal Darwin-width scaling with |cos2θ| gives about 28%, 12% and 5% losses. Si(111) energy width is about 1.3 × 10⁻⁴. The final design specifies intersection at the sample. The actual alignment criterion remains unconfirmed.

interactiveIdeas.title: Orientation and strain from diffraction spots
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors apply rotation, shear or uniform expansion to a crystal. Rotation changes all reflection directions together; shear changes their relative angles. Uniform expansion leaves directions unchanged but changes the monochromatic energy at which a reflection occurs.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Laue spot directions determine orientation and five shape-changing strain components. One energy measurement supplies overall expansion or contraction, completing the six-component tensor.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Spot direction depends on q/|q|. Uniform expansion changes |q| while preserving its direction. Deviatoric strain resolution is about 10⁻⁴, reaching 2 × 10⁻⁵ under favourable conditions. At 510 mm, a 200 µm pixel spans about 3.9 × 10⁻⁴ rad in 2θ and 2 × 10⁻⁴ in plane-normal direction and dd/d at 90°. Subpixel fitting over many reflections gives better precision. The preliminary rule of one pixel near 10⁻⁴ is a target, not exact at 0.51 m. Rotations near 0.01° are readily resolved. Add a reflection-energy measurement near 10⁻⁴ relative width for the dilatational strain component.

funFacts: The final-design nano mirrors require 0.4 to 0.5 nm root-mean-square shape accuracy for a roughly 40 nm focus.
A 100 mm aluminium part expands about 100 nm during a 0.04 °C temperature increase. The preliminary design specifies a 0.02 °C local thermal enclosure for the nano station.
Larson, Yang, Ice, Budai and Tischler introduced wire-based depth-resolved Laue diffraction at the APS in Nature in 2002. The method became a principal technique at 34-ID-E.
The pre-2009 End near focus photograph depicts a platinum wire about 50 µm thick, roughly 200 µm above the sample. Geometry files from 2022 and 2023 instead use 101.5 µm diameter.
The 256-bit gold mask contains every eight-bit subsequence once. Gursoy and colleagues' 2022 coded-aperture method adapts a principle used in X-ray astronomy.

The final design specifies a second monochromator crystal about 60 °C warmer than the first. Thermal expansion changes exit angle by roughly 0.02 to 0.13 mrad, more at lower energy. This is intended to align pink and single-energy illumination. The procedure for maintaining the same sub-100 nm spot is unpublished.
Most useful upper-detector signal is from 12 to 17 keV. At lower energies fewer reflections reach 90°; at higher energies intensity falls. This energy range is from the preliminary design.

The preliminary design reports high pre-upgrade beamtime demand. Successful 34-ID-E proposals typically needed a review score near 1.4, between extraordinary and excellent and closer to extraordinary.
Liu and colleagues demonstrated energy-independent mirror focusing to 85 × 95 nm at 15 keV in an APS User Meeting poster in 2005.

The preliminary-design gain budget multiplies a hundredfold brightness increase, ninefold mirror improvement, fivefold coded-aperture improvement and tenfold detector improvement. The largest combined estimate is 45,000-fold faster acquisition.
The 2024 computing strategy projects about 2.8 PB of raw data per year, roughly seven times pre-upgrade 34-ID-E output.
Shielded ATOMIC transport crosses 34-ID-E. The final design permits access to the 3DMN hutch during ATOMIC operation, with independent operation of both branches.
The former 34-ID-E used the inboard source. The final design assigns outboard 3DMN and inboard ATOMIC.
SharafEldin and colleagues' 2026 study applied unsupervised machine learning to 34-ID-E wire-scan volumes. It identified stainless-steel dislocation cells from data with 0.5 µm depth resolution.

openQuestions: The final design places the nano station at 65.5 m. No public 2024 to 2026 source confirms installation or commissioning. The 2024 computing strategy reports scope reductions including detector purchases, and APS updates describe delivery of infrastructure. The exhibit therefore treats the station as a design with unknown status. A December 2021 scope town hall has no public slides.

Installed detectors are unknown. Pre-upgrade instruments had a PerkinElmer XRD1621 top panel and two XRD0820 side panels. Planned Pilatus 6M-class and two 1 to 2 megapixel replacements were removed from the upgrade scope. The ATOMIC Eiger 500K directory entry applies to 34-ID-F. The August 2026 ModSim talk proposed tenfold faster collection without identifying a detector and mentioned wire reconstruction with Eiger.

As-built focal widths and fluxes are unpublished. Design ray traces at 14 keV give 103 × 68 nm micro and 37 × 37 nm nano. The directory lists 0.15 × 0.15 µm, 10¹⁴ pink photons/s and 10¹¹ monochromatic photons/s at 15 keV. MEDSI 2025 reports performance-criterion compliance but no 3DMN widths. Brightness and energy range were the criteria; only ISN had a focal-width criterion.
The final design gives 2.1 m for both canted devices, compared with the ATOMIC directory's 2.3 m revolver length. The 3DMN magnetic length lacks independent as-built confirmation.

The preliminary design proposed liquid-nitrogen-cooled silicon mirrors. The final design specifies three stripes, 3.0 mrad incidence and a deformation-reducing notch but omits coolant. The design documents agree on outboard 3DMN and inboard ATOMIC reflection, consistent with the approximately 0.4 m plan separation. As-built confirmation remains absent.

The final design describes pink and monochromatic beam intersection at the sample. Pateras and colleagues describe intersection at the final optics in the 34-ID-C predecessor. The mirrors are about 0.1 m from the focus, so these are similar alignment descriptions. Quantitatively, 2αΔT tanθB for 60 K gives about 20 to 125 µrad over 30 to 5.3 keV. Closing 1.1 mm over the approximately 6 m distance to micro mirrors requires 180 µrad, or 95 µrad over 11.7 m to nano mirrors. A crossing angle ψ also shifts focus by roughly ψq, potentially micrometres. The operating procedure for coincident sub-100 nm spots is unconfirmed, including temperature adjustment, mirror realignment and residual offset.

Enclosure dimensions are scaled from final-design Fig. 4.58, with about ±0.3 m longitudinal uncertainty and less certain widths. Label 34-ID-D is absent and appears incorporated into the expanded E enclosure.

The tabulated 60.0 and 65.5 m positions refer to instruments and mirrors. Actual focus depends on as-built focal lengths. Preliminary values are horizontal and vertical 70 and 142 mm micro, 55 and 120 mm nano, with working distances at least 50 mm and about 30 mm.

Routine post-upgrade use of wire or coded-mask depth scanning is unconfirmed. Coded apertures were demonstrated during 2022 to 2025; mask reconstruction was research prototyping in the 2024 computing strategy.
The undulator supports up to 5 mm gap taper. Its use for smoothing the post-upgrade Laue spectrum is undocumented.
Design energy range is 5.3 to 30 keV, compared with the current directory's 5.5 to 30 keV.

The 5 October 2026 chart lists scientific commissioning and early experiments at stage 5. General-user restart date at stage 6 is unannounced, although proposals are accepted. Early two-dimensional measurements ran around late July 2026; computing-intensive three-dimensional coded-mask experiments were planned for winter in the ModSim talk.
For partner ATOMIC, the first mirror pair is at 52.0 m in Table 4.63 and 54 m in text. The former 34-ID-E wiki gives source separation as 1 µrad, a unit error for 1 mrad.

Pre-upgrade pink-flux baselines differ. The preliminary design describes about 10¹⁴ photons/s as a fiftyfold increase over 500 nm operation. The 2016 web specification gives 10¹¹ white photons/s for the old station. These are inconsistent comparison baselines.

Pre-upgrade panel names differ among sources. The top is XRD 1621 in Das and colleagues and PE1621 in geometry files, but XRD 1620 AN in the 2024 computing strategy. Side panels are XRD 0820 AN on the Instruments page and computing strategy, or PE0822 in 2022 and 2023 geometry files. Generic PerkinElmer 2k × 2k and 1k × 1k amorphous-silicon panel descriptions avoid an unconfirmed model assignment.
